g3_tombstone_guard: No Q may depend on QAST, EWRA, P39, RT3, or a claim that G3 established a general method.

Q1.claim: Perturbations that preserve versus destroy a plan/subgoal boundary yield different repair topology/latency after matching state distance and motor burden.
Q1.fatal_rival: The effect is entirely generic surprise, motor interruption, or state-distance cost.
Q1.prospective_discriminator: presealed 2x2 perturbation relation-to-plan by state-distance/motor-burden factorial

Q2.claim: Learning includes discrete state-recognition/action-uncertainty/chunk transitions not reducible to monotone speedup.
Q2.fatal_rival: Practice, individual ability, and fixed-method memorization explain every apparent discontinuity.
Q2.prospective_discriminator: longitudinal state-conditioned entropy/transfer change points against timing-only and fixed-method controls

Q3.claim: Frame transformations impose separable spatial-transform, action-coordinate, and plan-continuity costs in sequential action.
Q3.fatal_rival: All cost is generic mental rotation, visual familiarity, or motor remapping.
Q3.prospective_discriminator: frame transform x action-label remap x plan continuity factorial

Q4.claim: Skilled non-shortest routes reflect a measurable objective beyond step length, not ignorance or a known method constraint.
Q4.fatal_rival: Knowledge, motor cost, and known method constraints fully explain the route gap.
Q4.prospective_discriminator: preselected exact states where latent cost models rank routes differently

Q5.claim: Transfer separates structural state/action knowledge from perceptual chunks, named algorithms, and generic practice.
Q5.fatal_rival: Difficulty, generic spatial ability, algorithm overlap, and order explain transfer.
Q5.prospective_discriminator: presealed shared-structure by shared-surface/action-vocabulary transfer matrix

Q6.claim: Recent legal action history causally biases next action after exact state, frame, and subgoal controls.
Q6.fatal_rival: Motor sequence bias, residual orientation, hidden subgoal, or incomplete state matching causes the association.
Q6.prospective_discriminator: history manipulation with exact state/frame/subgoal and motor-history controls
Q6.g3_role: high-overlap risk; no G3 dependency permitted

Q7.claim: Population performance changes are driven by discrete algorithm/knowledge adoption beyond practice, selection, hardware, and event-format effects.
Q7.fatal_rival: Selection, entry, hardware/format, practice curves, survivorship, and retrospective event matching explain the trend.
Q7.prospective_discriminator: presealed interrupted trend/event study with negative-control events and unaffected subevents

Q8.claim: Sighted/blindfold performance bottlenecks can be separated into state estimation, retrieval, working memory, motor execution, and algorithm knowledge.
Q8.fatal_rival: Population/repertoire/event-format differences and aggregate time make mechanisms unidentified.
Q8.prospective_discriminator: matched solver/task measures or factorial prospective tax of memory, estimation, and execution

freeze_rule: No candidate may be reworded after literature outcomes to evade a fatal rival.
